sanskrit: tad āpatad vai sahasā śalyasya sumahad balam mahaughavegaṃ samare vārayām āsa pāṇḍavaḥ
english: As Śalya's vast host came rushing on all at once, sweeping forward like the rush of a mighty flood, the son of Pāṇḍu held it back in the battle.

sanskrit: madrarājaṃ ca samare dharmarājo mahārathaḥ daśabhiḥ sāyakais tūrṇam ājaghāna stanāntare nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca tribhis tribhir ajihmagaiḥ
english: And the king of righteousness, that great chariot-warrior, swiftly struck the king of the Madras full in the chest with ten arrows in the fight; and Nakula and Sahadeva struck him each with three straight-flying shafts.

sanskrit: madrarājo 'pi tān sarvān ājaghāna tribhis tribhiḥ yudhiṣṭhiraṃ punaḥ ṣaṣṭyā vivyādha niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ mādrīputrau ca saṃrabdhau dvābhyāṃ dvābhyām atāḍayat
english: The king of the Madras in turn smote them all, each with three arrows, and pierced Yudhiṣṭhira again with sixty whetted shafts, and struck the two furious sons of Mādrī with two arrows apiece.

sanskrit: tato bhīmo mahābāhur dṛṣṭvā rājānam āhave madrarājavaśaṃ prāptaṃ mṛtyor āsyagataṃ yathā abhyadravata saṃgrāme yudhiṣṭhiram amitrajit
english: Then mighty-armed Bhīma, vanquisher of foes, seeing the king fallen into the power of the lord of the Madras in the battle, as if caught in the very jaws of death, rushed to Yudhiṣṭhira's side in the fray.

sanskrit: tato yuddhaṃ mahāghoraṃ prāvartata sudāruṇam aparāṃ diśam āsthāya dyotamāne divākare
english: Then a most terrible and savage combat broke out, while the sun, blazing, had taken its stand in the western quarter.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tataḥ pitā tava kruddho niśitaiḥ sāyakottamaiḥ ājaghāna raṇe pārthān sahasenān samantataḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then your father, filled with wrath, with his keen and excellent shafts struck the sons of Pṛthā along with their armies on every side in the battle.

sanskrit: bhīmaṃ dvādaśabhir viddhvā sātyakiṃ navabhiḥ śaraiḥ nakulaṃ ca tribhir bāṇaiḥ sahadevaṃ ca saptabhiḥ
english: He pierced Bhīma with twelve arrows and Sātyaki with nine shafts, Nakula with three darts and Sahadeva with seven,

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraṃ dvādaśabhir bāhvor urasi cārpayat dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ tato viddhvā vinanāda mahābalaḥ
english: and into Yudhiṣṭhira's arms and breast he drove twelve shafts; then, having pierced Dhṛṣṭadyumna, the mighty one roared aloud.

sanskrit: taṃ dvādaśārdhair nakulo mādhavaś ca tribhiḥ śaraiḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca saptatyā bhīmasenaś ca pañcabhiḥ yudhiṣṭhiro dvādaśabhiḥ pratyavidhyat pitāmaham
english: In return Nakula pierced the grandsire with six, and Mādhava with three shafts, Dhṛṣṭadyumna with seventy and Bhīmasena with five, while Yudhiṣṭhira struck back the grandsire with twelve.

sanskrit: droṇas tu sātyakiṃ viddhvā bhīmasenam avidhyata ekaikaṃ pañcabhir bāṇair yamadaṇḍopamaiḥ śitaiḥ
english: And Droṇa, having pierced Sātyaki, then struck Bhīmasena, smiting each with five sharp arrows like the rod of Yama.

sanskrit: tau ca taṃ pratyavidhyetāṃ tribhis tribhir ajihmagaiḥ tottrair iva mahānāgaṃ droṇaṃ brāhmaṇapuṃgavam
english: And those two struck him back, each with three straight-flying shafts, as men goad a great elephant with hooks—Droṇa, that bull among brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: sauvīrāḥ kitavāḥ prācyāḥ pratīcyodīcyamālavāḥ abhīṣāhāḥ śūrasenāḥ śibayo 'tha vasātayaḥ saṃgrāme nājahur bhīṣmaṃ vadhyamānāḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: The Sauvīras, the Kitavas, the men of the east and the west and the north, the Mālavas, the Abhīṣāhas, the Śūrasenas, the Śibis, and the Vasātis, though cut down by sharp arrows, did not abandon Bhīṣma in the fight.

sanskrit: tathaivānye vadhyamānāḥ pāṇḍaveyair mahātmabhiḥ pāṇḍavān abhyavartanta vividhāyudhapāṇayaḥ tathaiva pāṇḍavā rājan parivavruḥ pitāmaham
english: Likewise others too, though being slain by the high-souled men of the Pāṇḍava side, advanced against the Pāṇḍavas with weapons of every kind in their hands; and even so, O king, the Pāṇḍavas encircled the grandsire.

sanskrit: sa samantāt parivṛto rathaughair aparājitaḥ gahane 'gnir ivotsṛṣṭaḥ prajajvāla dahan parān
english: Surrounded on every side by floods of chariots, yet unconquered, he blazed forth like a fire let loose in a thicket, consuming the foe.

sanskrit: rathāgnyagāraś cāpārcir asiśaktigadendhanaḥ śarasphuliṅgo bhīṣmāgnir dadāha kṣatriyarṣabhān
english: His chariot was the fire-altar, his bow the flame, swords, lances, and maces its fuel, his arrows the sparks—and that fire that was Bhīṣma burned up the bulls among the warriors.

sanskrit: suvarṇapuṅkhair iṣubhir gārdhrapakṣaiḥ sutejanaiḥ karṇinālīkanārācaiś chādayām āsa tad balam
english: With gold-feathered arrows fledged with vulture-plumes and finely sharpened, with barbed shafts, nālīka darts, and iron bolts, he covered over that host.

sanskrit: apātayad dhvajāṃś caiva rathinaś ca śitaiḥ śaraiḥ muṇḍatālavanānīva cakāra sa rathavrajān
english: With his keen shafts he brought down banners and chariot-warriors alike, and made the ranks of chariots like groves of palm-trees stripped bare of their crowns.

sanskrit: nirmanuṣyān rathān rājan gajān aśvāṃś ca saṃyuge akarot sa mahābāhuḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: Chariots, elephants, and horses he left without men upon them in the battle, O king—that mighty-armed one, the foremost of all who bear arms.

sanskrit: tasya jyātalanirghoṣaṃ visphūrjitam ivāśaneḥ niśamya sarvabhūtāni samakampanta bhārata
english: Hearing the roar of his bowstring against the leather guard, like the crash of a thunderbolt, all creatures trembled, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: amoghā hy apatan bāṇāḥ pitus te bharatarṣabha nāsajjanta tanutreṣu bhīṣmacāpacyutāḥ śarāḥ
english: For your father's arrows fell never in vain, O bull of the Bharatas; the shafts loosed from Bhīṣma's bow were not stayed by any armor.

sanskrit: hatavīrān rathān rājan saṃyuktāñ javanair hayaiḥ apaśyāma mahārāja hriyamāṇān raṇājire
english: Chariots whose heroes had been slain, yet yoked still to swift horses, we beheld, O great king, being dragged across the field of battle.

sanskrit: cedikāśikarūṣāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi caturdaśa mahārathāḥ samākhyātāḥ kulaputrās tanutyajaḥ aparāvartinaḥ sarve suvarṇavikṛtadhvajāḥ
english: Fourteen thousand of the Cedis, Kāśis, and Karūṣas—renowned as great chariot-warriors, sons of noble houses, ready to give up their lives, all unflinching, with banners wrought of gold—

sanskrit: saṃgrāme bhīṣmam āsādya vyāditāsyam ivāntakam nimagnāḥ paralokāya savājirathakuñjarāḥ
english: having come upon Bhīṣma in the battle, like Death with jaws agape, sank down into the other world together with their horses, chariots, and elephants.

sanskrit: bhagnākṣopaskarān kāṃś cid bhagnacakrāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ apaśyāma rathān rājañ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Chariots with axles and frames shattered, some with their wheels broken all about, we beheld, O king, by the hundreds and by the thousands.

sanskrit: savarūthai rathair bhagnai rathibhiś ca nipātitaiḥ śaraiḥ sukavacaiś chinnaiḥ paṭṭiśaiś ca viśāṃ pate
english: With broken chariots and their canopies, with fallen chariot-warriors, with shattered fine coats of mail and arrows and spears, O lord of peoples,

sanskrit: gadābhir musalaiś caiva nistriṃśaiś ca śilīmukhaiḥ anukarṣair upāsaṅgaiś cakrair bhagnaiś ca māriṣa
english: with maces and pestles, with swords and bee-shaped shafts, with chariot-poles and quivers and broken wheels, O honored one,

sanskrit: bāhubhiḥ kārmukaiḥ khaḍgaiḥ śirobhiś ca sakuṇḍalaiḥ talatrair aṅgulitraiś ca dhvajaiś ca vinipātitaiḥ cāpaiś ca bahudhā chinnaiḥ samāstīryata medinī
english: with arms and bows and swords, with heads still bearing their earrings, with leathern wrist-guards and finger-guards, with fallen banners, and with bows cut to pieces in many places—with all these the earth was strewn over.

sanskrit: hatārohā gajā rājan hayāś ca hatasādinaḥ paripetur drutaṃ tatra śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Elephants whose riders had been slain and horses whose mounted men were dead ran wildly to and fro there, O king, by the hundreds and the thousands.

sanskrit: yatamānāś ca te vīrā dravamāṇān mahārathān nāśaknuvan vārayituṃ bhīṣmabāṇaprapīḍitān
english: And those heroes, though they strove their utmost, could not check the great chariot-warriors as they fled, tormented by Bhīṣma's arrows.

sanskrit: mahendrasamavīryeṇa vadhyamānā mahācamūḥ abhajyata mahārāja na ca dvau saha dhāvataḥ
english: Cut down by him whose valor equaled great Indra's, the mighty host broke and scattered, O great king, so that not even two men fled together.

sanskrit: āviddharathanāgāśvaṃ patitadhvajakūbaram anīkaṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ hāhābhūtam acetanam
english: With its chariots, elephants, and horses thrown into confusion, its banners and chariot-poles fallen, the army of the sons of Pāṇḍu became one cry of woe, bereft of its senses.

sanskrit: jaghānātra pitā putraṃ putraś ca pitaraṃ tathā priyaṃ sakhāyaṃ cākrande sakhā daivabalātkṛtaḥ
english: There, in the rout, father slew son and son slew father, and friend slew beloved friend, each driven on by the force of fate.

sanskrit: vimucya kavacān anye pāṇḍuputrasya sainikāḥ prakīrya keśān dhāvantaḥ pratyadṛśyanta bhārata
english: Others among the son of Pāṇḍu's soldiers cast off their armor and, with their hair flying loose, were seen running away, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tad gokulam ivodbhrāntam udbhrāntarathakuñjaram dadṛśe pāṇḍuputrasya sainyam ārtasvaraṃ tadā
english: Like a herd of cattle in a stampede, its chariots and elephants scattering in panic, the army of the son of Pāṇḍu was then to be seen, raising a cry of distress.

sanskrit: prabhajyamānaṃ sainyaṃ tu dṛṣṭvā yādavanandanaḥ uvāca pārthaṃ bībhatsuṃ nigṛhya ratham uttamam
english: Seeing the army being broken to pieces, the delight of the Yādavas reined in that excellent chariot and spoke to Pārtha, the Bībhatsu:

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa kālaḥ saṃprāptaḥ pārtha yaḥ kāṅkṣitas tava praharāsmai naravyāghra na cen mohāt pramuhyase
english: "This is the very hour, O Pārtha, that you have longed for; strike now at this man, O tiger among men—unless from bewilderment your purpose fails you.

sanskrit: yat purā kathitaṃ vīra tvayā rājñāṃ samāgame virāṭanagare pārtha saṃjayasya samīpataḥ
english: What you yourself once declared, O hero, before the assembled kings in Virāṭa's city, O Pārtha, in the presence of Saṃjaya—

sanskrit: bhīṣmadroṇamukhān sarvān dhārtarāṣṭrasya sainikān sānubandhān haniṣyāmi ye māṃ yotsyanti saṃyuge
english: 'All the warriors of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, with Bhīṣma and Droṇa at their head, together with their kinsmen, I shall slay—whoever shall give me battle in the fight'—

sanskrit: iti tat kuru kaunteya satyaṃ vākyam ariṃdama kṣatradharmam anusmṛtya yudhyasva bharatarṣabha
english: make good that word, O son of Kuntī, O subduer of foes; remembering the duty of a kṣatriya, do battle, O bull of the Bharatas."

sanskrit: ity ukto vāsudevena tiryagdṛṣṭir adhomukhaḥ akāma iva bībhatsur idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Thus addressed by Vāsudeva, the Bībhatsu, with sidelong glance and downcast face, as though against his will, spoke these words:

sanskrit: avadhyānāṃ vadhaṃ kṛtvā rājyaṃ vā narakottaram duḥkhāni vanavāse vā kiṃ nu me sukṛtaṃ bhavet
english: "By slaying those who ought not to be slain, what good can come to me—whether a kingdom that leads but to hell, or the sorrows of life in the forest?

sanskrit: codayāśvān yato bhīṣmaḥ kariṣye vacanaṃ tava pātayiṣyāmi durdharṣaṃ vṛddhaṃ kurupitāmaham
english: Drive on the horses to where Bhīṣma stands; I shall do your bidding. I shall bring down the unassailable old grandsire of the Kurus."

sanskrit: tato 'śvān rajataprakhyāṃś codayām āsa mādhavaḥ yato bhīṣmas tato rājan duṣprekṣyo raśmivān iva
english: Then Mādhava urged on the horses, white as silver, toward where Bhīṣma stood—who, O king, was hard to gaze upon, like the radiant sun.

sanskrit: tatas tat punar āvṛttaṃ yudhiṣṭhirabalaṃ mahat dṛṣṭvā pārthaṃ mahābāhuṃ bhīṣmāyodyantam āhave
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira's great host turned back again, seeing the mighty-armed Pārtha rising up against Bhīṣma in the battle.

sanskrit: tato bhīṣmaḥ kuruśreṣṭhaḥ siṃhavad vinadan muhuḥ dhanaṃjayarathaṃ śīghraṃ śaravarṣair avākirat
english: Then Bhīṣma, foremost of the Kurus, roaring again and again like a lion, swiftly overwhelmed Dhanaṃjaya's chariot with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: kṣaṇena sa rathas tasya sahayaḥ sahasārathiḥ śaravarṣeṇa mahatā na prājñāyata kiṃ cana
english: In an instant that chariot of his, with its horses and its driver, was so covered by the great rain of arrows that nothing of it could be made out at all.

sanskrit: vāsudevas tv asaṃbhrānto dhairyam āsthāya sātvataḥ codayām āsa tān aśvān vitunnān bhīṣmasāyakaiḥ
english: But Vāsudeva of the Sātvatas, unshaken, holding firm to his steadiness, urged on those horses that were wounded by Bhīṣma's shafts.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārtho dhanur gṛhya divyaṃ jaladanisvanam pātayām āsa bhīṣmasya dhanuś chittvā śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then Pārtha, taking up his divine bow that sounded like a thundercloud, cut Bhīṣma's bow with his keen shafts and brought it down.

sanskrit: sa cchinnadhanvā kauravyaḥ punar anyan mahad dhanuḥ nimeṣāntaramātreṇa sajyaṃ cakre pitā tava
english: His bow thus severed, that scion of Kuru, your father, in but the span between two blinks of an eye strung another great bow.

sanskrit: vicakarṣa tato dorbhyāṃ dhanur jaladanisvanam athāsya tad api kruddhaś ciccheda dhanur arjunaḥ
english: With both arms he drew that bow that roared like a thundercloud; but this one too the wrathful Arjuna cut through.

sanskrit: tasya tat pūjayām āsa lāghavaṃ śaṃtanoḥ sutaḥ sādhu pārtha mahābāho sādhu kuntīsuteti ca
english: The son of Śaṃtanu praised that swiftness of his: "Well done, O mighty-armed Pārtha! Well done, O son of Kuntī!"

sanskrit: samābhāṣyainam aparaṃ pragṛhya ruciraṃ dhanuḥ mumoca samare bhīṣmaḥ śarān pārtharathaṃ prati
english: Having so addressed him, Bhīṣma took up another splendid bow and loosed his arrows in the battle against Pārtha's chariot.

sanskrit: adarśayad vāsudevo hayayāne paraṃ balam moghān kurvañ śarāṃs tasya maṇḍalāni vidarśayan
english: Vāsudeva showed forth surpassing skill in the driving of the horses, making the other's arrows fall in vain by displaying his wheeling circles.

sanskrit: śuśubhāte naravyāghrau bhīṣmapārthau śarakṣatau govṛṣāv iva saṃrabdhau viṣāṇollikhitāṅkitau
english: Those two tigers among men, Bhīṣma and Pārtha, gashed by arrows, shone resplendent, like two furious bulls scored and marked by each other's horns.

sanskrit: vāsudevas tu saṃprekṣya pārthasya mṛduyuddhatām bhīṣmaṃ ca śaravarṣāṇi sṛjantam aniśaṃ yudhi
english: But Vāsudeva, beholding the gentleness of Pārtha's fighting, and Bhīṣma pouring forth showers of arrows unceasingly in the battle,

sanskrit: pratapantam ivādityaṃ madhyam āsādya senayoḥ varān varān vinighnantaṃ pāṇḍuputrasya sainikān
english: blazing like the sun as he stood between the two armies, striking down one after another the best of the son of Pāṇḍu's warriors,

sanskrit: yugāntam iva kurvāṇaṃ bhīṣmaṃ yaudhiṣṭhire bale nāmṛṣyata mahābāhur mādhavaḥ paravīrahā
english: making it seem as though the end of an age had come upon Yudhiṣṭhira's host—that Bhīṣma the mighty-armed Mādhava, slayer of hostile heroes, could no longer endure.

sanskrit: utsṛjya rajataprakhyān hayān pārthasya māriṣa kruddho nāma mahāyogī pracaskanda mahārathāt abhidudrāva bhīṣmaṃ sa bhujapraharaṇo balī
english: Letting go of Pārtha's horses, white as silver, O honored one, that great master of yoga, in his wrath, leapt down from the great chariot, and the mighty one rushed at Bhīṣma with only his arms for weapons.

sanskrit: pratodapāṇis tejasvī siṃhavad vinadan muhuḥ dārayann iva padbhyāṃ sa jagatīṃ jagatīśvaraḥ
english: Goad in hand, blazing with splendor, roaring again and again like a lion, that lord of the world seemed to rend the very earth with his feet.

sanskrit: krodhatāmrekṣaṇaḥ kṛṣṇo jighāṃsur amitadyutiḥ grasann iva ca cetāṃsi tāvakānāṃ mahāhave
english: His eyes red with wrath, eager to slay, of measureless brilliance, Kṛṣṇa seemed in that great battle to devour the very spirits of your men.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā mādhavam ākrande bhīṣmāyodyantam āhave hato bhīṣmo hato bhīṣma iti tatra sma sainikāḥ krośantaḥ prādravan sarve vāsudevabhayān narāḥ
english: Seeing Mādhava in the tumult rising up against Bhīṣma in the fight, the warriors there cried out, "Bhīṣma is slain! Bhīṣma is slain!" and all those men fled away in terror of Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: pītakauśeyasaṃvīto maṇiśyāmo janārdanaḥ śuśubhe vidravan bhīṣmaṃ vidyunmālī yathāmbudaḥ
english: Wrapped in yellow silk, dark as a sapphire, Janārdana, as he rushed upon Bhīṣma, shone resplendent like a thundercloud garlanded with lightning.

sanskrit: sa siṃha iva mātaṅgaṃ yūtharṣabha ivarṣabham abhidudrāva tejasvī vinadan yādavarṣabhaḥ
english: As a lion springs upon an elephant, or the bull of the herd upon a rival bull, so did that splendid bull of the Yādavas rush forward, roaring.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya puṇḍarīkākṣam āhave asaṃbhramaṃ raṇe bhīṣmo vicakarṣa mahad dhanuḥ uvāca cainaṃ govindam asaṃbhrāntena cetasā
english: Beholding the lotus-eyed one rushing upon him in the battle, Bhīṣma, unperturbed, drew his great bow in the fray and spoke to Govinda with an untroubled heart:

sanskrit: ehy ehi puṇḍarīkākṣa devadeva namo 'stu te mām adya sātvataśreṣṭha pātayasva mahāhave
english: "Come, come, O lotus-eyed one, O God of gods, homage be to you! Strike me down today, O best of the Sātvatas, in this great battle!

sanskrit: tvayā hi deva saṃgrāme hatasyāpi mamānagha śreya eva paraṃ kṛṣṇa loke 'muṣminn ihaiva ca saṃbhāvito 'smi govinda trailokyenādya saṃyuge
english: For if I be slain by you in the battle, O sinless god, the highest good alone shall be mine, O Kṛṣṇa, both in that world and in this; I am honored, O Govinda, this day before the three worlds, in the fight."

sanskrit: anvag eva tataḥ pārthas tam anudrutya keśavam nijagrāha mahābāhur bāhubhyāṃ parigṛhya vai
english: Then close behind, the mighty-armed Pārtha, running after Keśava, caught hold of him, seizing him fast with both his arms.

sanskrit: nigṛhyamāṇaḥ pārthena kṛṣṇo rājīvalocanaḥ jagāma cainam ādāya vegena puruṣottamaḥ
english: Though held back by Pārtha, the lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa, that supreme of men, dragging Arjuna along with him, still pressed forward with great force.

sanskrit: pārthas tu viṣṭabhya balāc caraṇau paravīrahā nijaghrāha hṛṣīkeśaṃ kathaṃ cid daśame pade
english: But Pārtha, slayer of hostile heroes, planting his feet firmly with all his strength, with great effort restrained Hṛṣīkeśa at the tenth step.

sanskrit: tata enam uvācārtaḥ krodhaparyākulekṣaṇam niḥśvasantaṃ yathā nāgam arjunaḥ paravīrahā
english: Then Arjuna, slayer of hostile heroes, in his distress spoke to him whose eyes were troubled with wrath, who hissed like a serpent:

sanskrit: nivartasva mahābāho nānṛtaṃ kartum arhasi yat tvayā kathitaṃ pūrvaṃ na yotsyāmīti keśava
english: "Turn back, O mighty-armed one! You must not make a falsehood of what you yourself declared before, that you would not fight, O Keśava.

sanskrit: mithyāvādīti lokas tvāṃ kathayiṣyati mādhava mamaiṣa bhāraḥ sarvo hi haniṣyāmi yatavratam
english: The world will call you a breaker of your word, O Mādhava. This whole burden is mine; I shall slay him who is steadfast in his vow.

sanskrit: śape mādhava sakhyena satyena sukṛtena ca antaṃ yathā gamiṣyāmi śatrūṇāṃ śatrukarśana
english: I swear, O Mādhava, by our friendship, by truth, and by my good deeds, that I shall make an end of the foes, O harrier of foes.

sanskrit: adyaiva paśya durdharṣaṃ pātyamānaṃ mahāvratam tārāpatim ivāpūrṇam antakāle yadṛcchayā
english: This very day behold the unassailable one, mighty in his vows, brought low—like the lord of the stars when, at the hour of doom, of itself it wanes and falls."

sanskrit: mādhavas tu vacaḥ śrutvā phalgunasya mahātmanaḥ nakiṃcid uktvā sakrodha āruroha rathaṃ punaḥ
english: And Mādhava, hearing the words of the high-souled Phalguna, said nothing, but, still wrathful, mounted the chariot again.

sanskrit: tau rathasthau naravyāghrau bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavaḥ punaḥ vavarṣa śaravarṣeṇa megho vṛṣṭyā yathācalau
english: Upon those two tigers among men, standing in their chariot, Bhīṣma the son of Śāntanu once more rained a rain of arrows, as a cloud pours its torrents upon two mountains.

sanskrit: prāṇāṃś cādatta yodhānāṃ pitā devavratas tava gabhastibhir ivādityas tejāṃsi śiśirātyaye
english: And your father Devavrata took the lives of the warriors as the sun with its rays draws up the dews at winter's end.

sanskrit: yathā kurūṇāṃ sainyāni babhañja yudhi pāṇḍavaḥ tathā pāṇḍavasainyāni babhañja yudhi te pitā
english: Even as the Pāṇḍava had broken the armies of the Kurus in the fight, so did your father break the armies of the Pāṇḍavas in the battle.

sanskrit: hatavidrutasainyās tu nirutsāhā vicetasaḥ nirīkṣituṃ na śekus te bhīṣmam apratimaṃ raṇe madhyaṃ gatam ivādityaṃ pratapantaṃ svatejasā
english: Their soldiers slain and put to flight, dispirited and bereft of their senses, they could not bear even to look upon the peerless Bhīṣma in the battle, blazing with his own splendor like the sun arrived at its zenith.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānā bhīṣmeṇa kāleneva yugakṣaye vīkṣāṃ cakrur mahārāja pāṇḍavā bhayapīḍitāḥ
english: Slain by Bhīṣma as if by Time itself at the dissolution of an age, the Pāṇḍavas, oppressed with fear, looked about them, O great king.
